## Tours to Victoria Island: choosing an itinerary through Bariloche

[Victoria Island](/argentina/place/victoria-island-nahuel-huapi/) lies among mountains and forested shores on [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/), near [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/). It can be reached by boat excursion. On many itineraries, the island visit is paired with a walk through the [Arrayanes myrtle forest](/argentina/place/arrayanes-forest/), where old trees have strikingly smooth orange-brown bark.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include the island on their main routes. **The main consideration is how much time is actually allocated to the catamaran and walks ashore**, and what else is scheduled in Bariloche that day. The [Victoria Island page](/argentina/place/victoria-island-nahuel-huapi/) covers the nature reserve in detail; here we compare the travel itineraries that include it.

The island is suited to a relaxed nature excursion rather than strenuous trekking. Yet two tours both featuring "Victoria Island" can be quite different: one visits after a flight, another combines the island with a long scenic drive, and a third allocates a separate day.

## Six Ada Tours journeys: differences in their itineraries

Victoria Island appears both in Argentina-focused journeys and in multi-country itineraries. One useful comparison is where the catamaran trip falls in the schedule:

| Tour | Victoria Island visit |
|---|---|
| [Best of Argentina, 14 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) | Day 9, two excursions in one day |
| [Chile and Argentina Deluxe, 14 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/) | Day 8, after arrival by air in Bariloche |
| [Argentina, Chile and Bolivia, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) | Island mentioned on days 15 and 16 |
| [Argentina and Patagonia, 26 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) | Day 14, after arrival in Bariloche |
| [Chile and Argentina VIP, 26 days](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/) | Day 14, group catamaran |

### Two 14-day routes: the island and Circuito Chico on the same day

Day 9 of the ["Best of Argentina" tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) is arranged in a similar way: a sightseeing drive around the lakeshore followed by a separate boat excursion. In this itinerary, both activities take place **in a group with an English-speaking guide**. Their sequence and whether both can be completed on the same day are confirmed at booking. This is an important specific qualification: two activities on a schedule do not guarantee any desired order regardless of catamaran operations.

Both options suit travelers who want to see Bariloche's panoramas from land and its island forests from the water in a single day. Combining the road and water excursions requires coordination, though, so compare the actual daily schedule rather than only the total length of the tour.

### "Chile and Argentina Deluxe": sailing after a flight

On the [14-day "Chile and Argentina Deluxe" tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/), Victoria Island and Arrayanes are scheduled for **day 8, in the afternoon after a flight from El Calafate**. Arrival is followed by a welcome and transfer to the hotel. This arrangement lets travelers experience the lake on the same day they change cities.

The key consideration here is the dependence on flight timings. This should not be treated as equivalent to a whole free day on the lake. If spending more time on the island matters to you, compare itineraries with a dedicated sailing day.

### Longer journeys of 18 and 26 days

The [18-day Argentina, Chile and Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-bolivia-cruise-tour-18-days/) combines high-altitude regions, southern Patagonia and Bariloche. Its description **mentions Victoria Island and Arrayanes Forest on two consecutive days, days 15 and 16**. One day has a Circuito Chico drive followed by a boat trip, while the next describes a catamaran to the island and forest. Clarify this repetition when confirming the itinerary: the text does not establish unambiguously how many separate catamaran trips are included.

In the [26-day "All of Argentina and Patagonia" journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), the catamaran to Victoria Island and Arrayanes Forest is planned for **day 14 after a flight from Mendoza to Bariloche**. A separate road sightseeing day in the lake district follows later. The lake and road experiences are thus spread across different days, although the overall trip is considerably longer.

The [26-day "Chile and Argentina VIP" tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/) assigns **day 14** to the island. It explicitly specifies **a group catamaran excursion lasting about 3 hours** and visiting Victoria Island and Arrayanes. Day 16 includes a Circuito Chico drive, after which the journey continues toward Salta. "VIP" in the tour title does not turn a group catamaran into a private one: each activity's format is defined by the itinerary's terms.

## Victoria Island and Arrayanes Forest: two different places

The names often appear together in boat-excursion descriptions, making them easy to mistake for a single natural landmark. In fact, [Victoria Island](/argentina/place/victoria-island-nahuel-huapi/) lies within Lake Nahuel Huapi, while [Arrayanes Forest](/argentina/place/arrayanes-forest/) occupies part of the Quetrihué Peninsula near [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/).

On the island, travelers disembark and walk along permitted forest paths. Native and introduced tree species grow here, with views over the lake and surrounding mountains from the shores. At Arrayanes, the central attraction is the tall myrtle trees with smooth, warm-colored trunks. Unlike the island, the forest is on a peninsula and can also be reached by other routes, including an overland approach from Villa La Angostura.

The classic excursion from Bariloche may depart from Puerto Pañuelo near the Llao Llao peninsula. However, **this well-known departure point does not automatically determine transport arrangements or the exact start time of each Ada Tours itinerary**. Follow the confirmed services, meeting point and timetable of the particular tour you choose.

## Circuito Chico and the catamaran: why the order matters

Circuito Chico introduces [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) from the lakeside road. Depending on the program, it may include [Playa Bonita](/argentina/place/playa-bonita/), [Cerro Campanario](/argentina/place/cerro-campanario/) and lookout points on the Llao Llao peninsula. From the catamaran, you see lakeshores, islands and mountains from the water, and spend part of the excursion walking on the island or through the forest.

When both activities appear on the same day, treat them as **two separate excursions, each with its own duration**. Several itineraries allow approximately four hours for Circuito Chico, while the boating portion depends on the sailing and number of stops. Weather, flight arrival times and travel to the dock also affect how easily the two can be combined.

Itineraries with separate days allow more unhurried exploration of the lake district. Combining the scenic drive and boat excursion in one day, on the other hand, leaves more time for glaciers, the Andes or several countries. Neither format is inherently better; the choice depends on the priorities of the whole trip.

## When to go and how to prepare for the boat trip

Bariloche's official tourism information describes excursions to Victoria Island and Arrayanes as available **year-round**, subject to actual weather and navigation conditions. Cold winds can sweep across the lake even in warmer months. Bring a windproof jacket for the catamaran and comfortable non-slip shoes for disembarking.

Southern Hemisphere summer is December–February and winter is June–August. Summer generally provides more daylight for walks; winter can mean cold, precipitation and changes to excursion routes. The fact that tickets are sold does not guarantee departure in all weather.

Check ahead which services are included in the particular product: transfer to the dock, catamaran ticket, access to the protected area, guide and meals. **Terms from one itinerary must not be assumed to apply to another.** For example, group sailing is expressly specified for the 26-day VIP journey; this does not imply a private catamaran.

## Choosing a tour that visits Victoria Island

If Bariloche is your principal destination, compare the days spent specifically in the region. Travelers who want to see the island and main viewpoints in one day may prefer a tour combining the catamaran with Circuito Chico. For a more relaxed schedule, look for a separate boating day. If you intend to visit several countries, evaluate the broader geography and necessary flights first.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_argentina_best_14_days,tour_source_chili_argentina,tour_source_kruiznyj_tur_po_luchshim_mestam_argentiny_chili_i_bolivii,tour_source_vsya_argentina,tour_source_chili_i_argentina_vip}}

This selection shows itineraries where Victoria Island is part of the main program. For more on the region, read about [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/) and [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/). For a wider choice, browse [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Victoria Island tours

### Do you need to stay overnight on the island?

**None of the active programs reviewed specifies an overnight stay on Victoria Island.** This is an excursion stop: afterward travelers return to Bariloche or continue according to their itinerary.

### Is Arrayanes Forest included in all six tours?

It is named in the itineraries of all six journeys under consideration, but the visit and its duration depend on the particular day. As the island and forest are separate places, confirm the content of the boat excursion when arranging the tour.

### How long does the catamaran trip take?

There is no single duration for every itinerary. The 26-day "Chile and Argentina VIP" tour specifies **about 3 hours of group sailing**. Bariloche's official tourism site generally offers trips to Victoria Island and Arrayanes ranging from half-day to full-day depending on the operator.

### Can you combine Victoria Island with Cerro Campanario?

Yes. Some 14-day itineraries pair a catamaran trip with Circuito Chico, which includes [Cerro Campanario](/argentina/place/cerro-campanario/). The actual order and feasibility of the full day depend on schedules.

### Is the excursion suitable for people who do not trek?

Yes. The standard boat excursion is intended for a broad range of visitors and includes walks on prepared or permitted paths. The length of walking sections and access to particular routes should be checked against the chosen tour and national park requirements.

## Villa La Angostura: lakes, Arrayanes Forest and Patagonia's mountain roads

Villa La Angostura stands on the shore of Lake Nahuel Huapi in Neuquén Province. This small mountain town is surrounded by forests, bays and slopes in northern Argentine Patagonia. Unlike the larger tourism center of [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), it is particularly well suited to relaxed lakeside walks, a dedicated day in the forest and journeys through the lake district.

Two natural attractions stand out nearby. One is the unusual arrayán myrtle trees on the Quetrihué Peninsula. The other is the drive known as the **Seven Lakes Route**, where lakeshores, forests and mountains change as you travel.

## Arrayanes Forest: what makes it different from other Patagonian forests?

[Los Arrayanes National Park](/argentina/place/arrayanes-forest/) protects a section of woodland on the Quetrihué Peninsula where trees have smooth cinnamon-colored bark. Official information from Argentina's national parks authority mentions centuries-old arrayán specimens. They form a distinctive canopy, with sunlight filtering onto the twisting trunks below.

There are two fundamentally different ways to visit. You can travel by boat across the lake to the forest area, or follow a long trail overland along the peninsula. Argentina's national tourism portal describes a walking route of around 12 km. Before choosing it, consider your fitness, available time, weather and return arrangements. **A short walk on wooden boardwalks among the trees and hiking the full length of the peninsula involve very different levels of effort.**

Check protected-area access arrangements and transport availability with the park and operator. Being based in the lakeside town does not itself mean that admission tickets, a catamaran trip or a guide are included.

## Lake Nahuel Huapi and other shores near town

[Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/) is a large glacial lake that connects Bariloche and Villa La Angostura. Different bays offer views of the water and forested mountains; even brief stops along the shore show the variety of Patagonia's lake district.

Nearby sights include the Correntoso River and lake, local beaches and viewpoints. On a hot day the clear water may make the place seem like a warm beach resort, but mountain lakes remain cool. For swimming, kayaking or boat trips, choose permitted locations and suitable conditions rather than assuming the whole shore is equally safe.

The region also has hiking trails of varying lengths. When choosing one, the real duration, elevation gain and forecast matter more than the number of stops you can fit into a day. Even a relatively short mountain walk after rain may require sturdier footwear.

## The Seven Lakes Route: where does it begin and what can you see?

The classic **Villa La Angostura–San Martín de los Andes** journey follows an approximately 110 km section of National Route 40. The city's official tourism portal lists Lakes Espejo, Correntoso, Escondido, Villarino, Falkner, Machónico and Lácar. The road features viewpoints, short walking stops and stretches of mountain forest.

| Stop | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Espejo | Water and panoramic views |
| Correntoso | Shoreline and a short walk |
| Falkner | Lake bordered by forested slopes |
| Lácar | Approach to San Martín |

You can drive the route simply to get from one place to another, but then your experience of its shores will be limited to views through the window. Allow more time for photographs, lakeside stops and leisurely walks than a navigation app estimates for a nonstop drive. Check road conditions before setting out in snowy, icy or very windy weather.

## Bariloche or Villa La Angostura: where should you stay?

[Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) offers a wider choice of urban activities, excursions and transport. Villa La Angostura is especially attractive if you value quiet lakeshores, forest paths, short nature stops and access to the Quetrihué Peninsula.

If time is tight, you can drive through both towns on one lakeside itinerary. But stopping for lunch and exploring the arrayán forest properly are different experiences. For the latter, leave enough time and decide in advance how you will get there and back.

On the [26-day grand tour of Argentina](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Villa La Angostura features during the lake-district stage along with Bariloche and Correntoso. It forms part of a longer journey across the country. Evaluate extra walks, boat trips and trekking against what is actually stated for the selected day, rather than a general list of regional activities.

## How the seasons change the trip

In the Southern Hemisphere's warmer months, longer walks and drives along lake roads are easier to plan. Autumn brings particularly appealing forest colors, but shorter days. In winter the mountains are known for snow and winter sports, which call for different clothing, travel arrangements and possible trail restrictions.

Even in summer, bring a waterproof jacket, warm layer and comfortable shoes. Temperatures on the water and in forest shade can be lower than on a sunny town street. Before hiking the peninsula, check which routes are accessible, return transport schedules and the wind forecast for the lake.

## Frequently asked questions about Villa La Angostura

### Can you see Arrayanes Forest without a long hike?

Yes. The official tourism portal describes access to the park by boat. Confirm operating times, departures and specific vessels before traveling.

### Is the Seven Lakes Route inside a national park?

Parts of it pass through the protected areas of Nahuel Huapi and Lanín. It is a mountain road with stops, not one continuous prepared hiking trail.

### Can you combine Villa La Angostura with Bariloche?

Yes. Both towns are connected by Lake Nahuel Huapi and roads. On a short visit, choose your main nature experience: Arrayanes Forest, the lakeshores or the longer route toward San Martín.

### How many days should you allow for Villa La Angostura?

Part of a day is enough for an overview, but several days are more sensible for Arrayanes Forest, unhurried lakeside exploration and the Seven Lakes Route, taking travel arrangements into account.

## Which tours pass through Villa La Angostura?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that include [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/) in the main itinerary. This small town lies on Lake Nahuel Huapi in Argentina's Neuquén Province. There is a practical reason to include it on an extended trip: the area brings together views of lakes and wooded mountains in northern Patagonia, with a road linking [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) to other lake valleys.

Ada Tours currently includes the town on the 14-day ["Chile & Argentina Deluxe"](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/) and the [26-day "Argentina and Patagonia Tour"](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). Both feature Villa La Angostura **as part of a full-day road excursion from Bariloche**, returning to Bariloche in the evening. Neither itinerary specifies an overnight stay in the town.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_chili_argentina,tour_source_vsya_argentina}}

## When and how is the town visited?

### Chile & Argentina Deluxe: day 9

Following the Chilean portion of the 14-day journey and Patagonia's glaciers, the itinerary reaches Bariloche. On **day 9**, a full-day excursion along lake roads takes place with an English-speaking guide and private transport. The route passes through the Limay River valley, a natural formation known as the Amphitheater, the Cuyín Manzano area and Lake Traful. After stops at the lake and [Villa Traful](/argentina/place/villa-traful/), the road continues to Villa La Angostura and the shores of Correntoso. Travelers return to Bariloche in the evening.

The experience is a succession of different landscapes: river valleys, rocky outcrops, lakeshores and forest. The excursion's "Seven Lakes" title does not automatically mean that the group covers every kilometer of the classic road to San Martín de los Andes. The confirmed stops are listed in the [tour itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/).

### Argentina and Patagonia, 26 days: day 15

On the longer journey, **day 15** is devoted to the "Circuito Grande" excursion from Bariloche. After driving alongside the Limay and stopping at the natural Amphitheater, travelers visit the Traful viewpoint and Villa Traful, where the description allocates time for lunch and local treats. The route then follows the lakeshore to Villa La Angostura, with views of Correntoso along the way. It is a full-day excursion with an English-speaking guide and private transport, ending back in Bariloche.

The drive forms part of a major journey featuring Buenos Aires, Iguazú, wine-producing areas, glaciers, El Chaltén and Ushuaia. Villa La Angostura therefore serves a particular purpose: introducing **Patagonia's lake district**, which is very different from Argentina's high-altitude north and the glaciers of the south. Full terms, duration and pricing appear on the [26-day journey page](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/).

## The Seven Lakes Route and Circuito Grande: why they are different

The classic Camino de los Siete Lagos is an approximately 110 km stretch of National Route 40 between Villa La Angostura and San Martín de los Andes. It passes Lakes Espejo, Correntoso, Escondido, Villarino, Falkner, Machónico and Lácar. Other bodies of water lie near the route, so a northern Patagonia journey can be **a lake-district drive** while following a different sequence of stops.

Circuito Grande from Bariloche is a separate driving loop through the Limay Valley, the Lake Traful area and Villa La Angostura. This is the geography described in the Ada Tours itineraries. It works well for a full day focused on changing scenery and several stops rather than moving from one hotel base to another.

If your goal is to drive the entire classic route to San Martín de los Andes, choose a program that **explicitly lists that drive** rather than assuming it from "Seven Lakes" in the day's title. On these two published Ada Tours trips, this section ends with a return to Bariloche.

## What else can you see in Villa La Angostura with more time?

Nearby sights include the shores of [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/), the Quetrihué Peninsula and [Arrayanes myrtle forest](/argentina/place/arrayanes-forest/). Arrayán trees have smooth brownish bark; visits on foot or by boat follow permitted routes within the national park. Other attractions for a separate stay include viewpoints, the shoreline and the Cerro Bayo mountain area.

**These are possibilities for extending your journey independently, not promised stops on the two listed tours.** Their lake-district day specifically confirms the drive through Traful and Villa La Angostura before returning to Bariloche. A long trek across Quetrihué, a skiing program or an additional lake cruise must not be assumed to be part of it.

For a fuller account of local natural sights and walks, see the [Villa La Angostura guide](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/). Here, the more important question is how much time the tour actually allocates to the town.

## Choosing between the two journeys

| Your priority | Suggested choice |
|---|---|
| Combine Chile, glaciers and lakes | 14-day itinerary |
| See more Argentine regions and southern Patagonia | 26-day itinerary |
| Visit Villa La Angostura and Traful | Both include stops |
| Stay several nights beside the lake | Requires a separate itinerary |

Both tours make the lake-district excursion from Bariloche. The difference lies **in the overall journey**, not a promise of an exclusive attraction inside Villa La Angostura. The 14-day tour concentrates more on combining Chile and Argentina; the 26-day journey adds a longer route through several parts of South America. Compare other country combinations in the [multi-country travel catalog](/multi-country/).

If you want to spend two or three full days here, the arrangements change: you need separate accommodation, time for Quetrihué or lakeside walks, and a plan to link them with Bariloche and Route 40. A town's presence among a tour's main destinations **does not itself mean that accommodation is provided there**.

## Roads, weather and the pace of the excursion

Nahuel Huapi National Park recommends preparing for changeable weather: even in summer the mountains can be windy and wet, while winter routes may require special vehicle preparation. On the two Ada Tours excursions, the transport and accompanying guide are specified; neither itinerary expects travelers to drive themselves.

Much of the day is devoted to driving and scenic stops. Distinguish the time spent walking from the total length of the excursion: both itineraries describe **a road-based day**, without a separate long trek at Villa La Angostura. Layered clothing and walking shoes are useful for photographs, brief viewpoint visits and changing temperatures.

## Questions about tours through Villa La Angostura

### Do these tours include an overnight stay in Villa La Angostura?

No. Both current itineraries include the town on a day excursion from Bariloche and return in the evening. Staying here would require a separate itinerary change.

### Is this the same as the complete Seven Lakes Route?

Not necessarily. Ada Tours visits Lake Traful and Villa La Angostura, while the classic Seven Lakes Route is the specific stretch of Route 40 ending in San Martín de los Andes. Look at the stops listed for the actual day.

### Can you see Villa Traful too?

Yes. Both listed itineraries include [Villa Traful](/argentina/place/villa-traful/) and a viewpoint above the lake. Tours passing through it are shown in a [separate catalog](/argentina/place/villa-traful/tour/).

### Which tour is better if the lakes are your main interest?

Both provide a full-day road excursion visiting Villa La Angostura. Choose according to the rest of the itinerary and its overall duration; a multi-day lakeside stay requires a different travel plan.

## Villa Traful: lake, forests and tranquil Patagonia

Villa Traful is in Argentine Patagonia, Neuquén Province, beside Lake Traful. Andean forests of cypress and coihue surround the shoreline, mountain slopes rise above the water, and the village's small cluster of buildings sits near the lake. It is an ideal stop on a journey through northern Patagonia's lake district when you want to leave the car, take a walk by the water and experience nature away from city bustle.

The area is part of Nahuel Huapi National Park. Visiting Villa Traful complements time in [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/) and at [Lake Nahuel Huapi](/argentina/place/nahuel-huapi-lake/), but each destination has its own appeal. Traful is especially memorable for its small lakeside village, scenic approach road and opportunities for a quiet day outdoors.

## What to see around Lake Traful

Mirador del Viento is a good first stop. From this lookout, you see the long lake, wooded slopes and mountain outlines. Winds can be strong, so approach the edges of viewing areas only where permitted. The color of the water changes with the light, and even on overcast days the shore and forest are inviting for walks and photographs.

Another famous attraction is **Traful's submerged forest**, Bosque Sumergido. Here, dried tree trunks rise out of the lake. This is not an ordinary forest path you can explore on foot: visitors usually reach the site by boat, and underwater activities call for special training and appropriate conditions. Check boat-tour availability for your dates, taking wind and local operators' schedules into account.

Nearby trails lead to waterfalls and forest areas. The national park authority describes, among others, a route to the cascades of the Catarata stream, starting roughly 7 km west of the village on Provincial Route 65. This hike has its own conditions and recommended season, so confirm that the trail is open before setting out.

## Getting there and how much time to allow

The main road approach is Provincial Route 65, which reaches Villa Traful through mountainous forested terrain. Official tourism information puts the village at around 100 km from both Bariloche and San Martín de los Andes, but actual travel times depend on the road chosen, surface conditions, weather and stops.

| Length of stop | What you can do |
|---|---|
| A few hours | Village, lakeshore and viewpoint |
| Full day | Scenic lookouts and a walk nearby |
| Overnight | Lake, trails and a relaxed stay |

Winter can bring snow, ice and trail closures. A wider range of walks is possible in the warmer season, although mountain winds and precipitation can change quickly. Bring closed shoes, warm outerwear and allow extra time for the drive. Before trekking in the national park, confirm registration requirements and trail availability.

On our [26-day itinerary through Argentina and neighboring countries](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Villa Traful is visited during a driving day, with a stop at a lakeside viewpoint and time for lunch. This is **a visit within a longer itinerary**; the submerged forest boat excursion and independent trekking do not become included services simply because the village is mentioned.

## How Villa Traful differs from other lake-district stops

[Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) has more urban infrastructure, while [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/) provides access to other parts of the lake district. Villa Traful is appealing for its combination of a small village, views over a long mountain lake and the chance to linger by the water.

If your journey allows only a short day, decide on your main priority: the panorama from the road, a leisurely walk or a boat trip. Trying to combine all three with a long drive and several distant lakes leaves little time to enjoy the places themselves.

## Frequently asked questions about Villa Traful

### Is Villa Traful on the Seven Lakes Route?

It is often included in broader road journeys through Patagonia's lake district. The village requires a separate approach via Provincial Route 65, so plan the detour and extra time deliberately.

### Can you see the submerged forest from shore?

It is a lake attraction. To explore Bosque Sumergido properly, visitors generally take a boat trip rather than an ordinary lakeside stroll. How it can be visited depends on weather and permitted local services.

### When is the best time to visit Villa Traful?

The Southern Hemisphere's warmer months are generally more convenient for walking and lake views. Winter brings different scenery, but snow and road conditions can restrict access to some places.

### Is it worth staying overnight?

An overnight stay is useful if you want to take walks, enjoy a quiet evening beside the lake and allow flexibility for changing weather. A brief road-tour stop can fit into part of a day if travel logistics allow.

## Which Ada Tours journeys pass through Villa Traful?

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with a scheduled visit to [Villa Traful](/argentina/place/villa-traful/). The village stands on Lake Traful in Nahuel Huapi National Park, Argentina's Neuquén Province. For travelers covering several South American regions, it offers a quieter side of Patagonia's lake district: wooded slopes, an expanse of lake water, a clifftop viewpoint and a tiny settlement among the mountains.

The place features on two current itineraries: the 14-day ["Chile & Argentina Deluxe"](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-deluxe/) and the [26-day "Argentina and Patagonia Tour"](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). On both, the Traful visit takes place **during a single sightseeing day departing from Bariloche**. Travelers stop at the village en route to [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/), then return to Bariloche. Neither tour specifies independent accommodation on the lakeshore.

## What does the Lake Traful excursion day look like?

The route crosses northwestern Patagonia, where lakes sit between forest-covered mountain ridges. Nahuel Huapi National Park describes the driving route known as Circuito Grande as a loop from Bariloche through the Limay River valley, the confluence of the Limay and Traful rivers, Provincial Route 65, Mirador del Viento, Villa Traful and a connection to Route 40. This explains how travelers can visit Traful in one busy day while seeing several distinct valleys.

### On the 14-day tour: day 9

On **day 9** of "Chile & Argentina Deluxe", a full-day "Seven Lakes" excursion is scheduled with an English-speaking guide and private transport. After the Limay Valley, the Amphitheater and Cuyín Manzano area, the group arrives at Lake Traful and its viewpoint. Then comes a stop in the village, with an opportunity for lunch and local chocolate or homemade sweets. The route continues to Villa La Angostura and Lake Correntoso, returning to [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) in the evening.

This is a day centered on **the drive and the views**, with several stops and changing landscapes. The itinerary confirms a viewpoint stop and a visit to the village. A separate boat trip on Lake Traful or a dive to the submerged forest is not included in the day's description.

### On the 26-day tour: day 15

On the [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), **day 15** is devoted to a Circuito Grande excursion with an English-speaking guide and private transport. Leaving Bariloche, the road follows the Limay, passes the natural Amphitheater and continues to Lake Traful and its viewpoint. Travelers then stop in Villa Traful: the description allocates time for lunch, tea, local chocolate and homemade sweets. The route continues to Villa La Angostura, passes Correntoso and returns to Bariloche.

On the longer journey, Traful is one stage of a wide-ranging itinerary through Argentina's wine regions, northern provinces, glacial and lake-district Patagonia. The aim of the day is **to introduce northern Patagonia without changing the overnight base**, as travelers continue to other parts of the country afterward.

## Why stop at the Traful viewpoint?

Mirador del Viento stands on a rocky outcrop high above the lake. From here you can see its long stretch of water, peninsulas and wooded mountainsides. The national park authority and Argentina's geological service both describe the lookout as a well-known attraction on the road to the village. It is raised above the shore, providing a different experience from walking along the water.

Both Ada Tours itineraries **explicitly include** a stop at this viewpoint. It is one of the few specific points on this driving day that can confidently be called part of both products. From above, the regional geography becomes clearer: the road runs high over the lake before descending to the village.

Wind and weather can change rapidly at Patagonian viewpoints. A windbreaker, non-slip shoes and layered clothing are useful for short stops out of the car. Do not infer the presence of barriers or access to a particular path on a given day from the description of an extended tour; actual access depends on local conditions.

## Lake Traful's submerged forest: is it included?

Near Villa Traful is the famous **submerged forest**, where tree trunks remain beneath the lake's surface. Argentina's tourism authorities describe the site as a destination for diving and boat trips. It is indeed an attraction for visitors who want to spend more time here.

However, **activities available in the region** are different from **services already purchased as part of a tour**. Neither the 14-day nor the 26-day itinerary promises scuba diving, a boat excursion to the forest, kayak rental or fishing specifically at Traful. Both clearly specify the driving excursion, panoramas, viewpoint and village stop.

If exploring the submerged forest, going boating or spending the day fishing is your main goal, plan a separate stay and check which services are actually offered. The driving route provides an introduction to the lake, whereas a specialized activity requires another itinerary and more time.

Both places appear on the same day of each tour, but offer different experiences.

| Place | Main role in the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Villa Traful | Lake, viewpoint and village |
| Villa La Angostura | Lakeshores and onward road |

At Villa Traful, travelers view the lake from above and stop in the small village. At [Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/), they see another part of the lake district, near Correntoso and Nahuel Huapi. [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) remains the base for these tours, with morning departures and evening returns.

For travelers interested in the second village, there is a [separate selection of tours visiting Villa La Angostura](/argentina/place/villa-la-angostura/tour/). The itineraries currently overlap, but the pages focus on different details: this one explores the Traful section, while the other explains Villa La Angostura's role and its connection to the Seven Lakes Route.

## Which itinerary should you choose for Traful?

Both tours include the relevant driving day. The deciding factor is therefore **the rest of the geography**. The 14-day itinerary connects Chile and Argentina, including glaciers and Bariloche's lake district. The 26-day journey is much broader, covering additional regions of Argentina and several neighboring countries. There is no reason to choose the longer tour solely in the hope of a longer stop in Villa Traful: both descriptions refer to one excursion day, not a multi-day village stay.

If you want to explore the lake at a relaxed pace, a separate lake-district itinerary with accommodation makes more sense. You could then divide time among lakeside walks, viewpoints and water activities according to the season. On the two current tours, time at Traful is limited by the excursion schedule, which also includes other stops.

## Practical questions

### How much time is allocated to Villa Traful on these tours?

Both include the village **on a single sightseeing day from Bariloche**. The exact time spent at the stop is not stated separately. The descriptions allow time for lunch or tea, but that does not mean several hours of free time by the lake.

### Is Traful on the Seven Lakes Route?

Lake Traful is in the same lake region of Nahuel Huapi National Park, but the classic Seven Lakes Route follows Route 40 from Villa La Angostura to San Martín de los Andes. The Traful road is an important separate loop and part of Circuito Grande. Thus "Seven Lakes" in the excursion title does not specify the complete list of stops.

### Can you see the submerged forest without diving?

Argentine tourism information describes opportunities to see the submerged forest area on boat trips. However, neither a boat trip nor diving at the forest is **automatically included** in the two tours discussed here.

### Is an overnight stay in Villa Traful included?

Both published itineraries return to Bariloche after visiting the village. A specially designed alternative itinerary is needed to stay overnight in Villa Traful.
